headline: HERTHA METALS BREAKS GROUND ON $100M TEXAS IRON PLANT — DOMESTIC SUPPLY CHAIN FOR US NEODYMIUM MAGNETS TAKES SHAPE
snippet: Hertha Metals has commenced construction of its commercial high-purity iron production plant in Texas, targeting early 2028 production. The $100 million facility will produce high-purity iron — a critical input for neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) permanent magnets used in EV motors and wind turbines — establishing a domestic US source to reduce dependence on Chinese supply chains. The move comes as the US magnetics supply chain faces pressure following China's June 2026 export controls on rare earth processing chemicals.

headline: CHINA HOLDS VETO ON $54B ANGLO-TECK MERGER — BEIJING DEMANDS COPPER SUPPLY VOLUMES, NOT ASSET SALES, FROM SAMR REVIEW
snippet: China's SAMR has told Anglo American that copper concentrate supply volume commitments — not asset divestitures — are its condition for approving the $54 billion Anglo-Teck merger, according to Reuters sources. The combined entity would control only about 5% of global copper supply, yet China's effective veto power stems from its role as the world's largest copper consumer. Anglo American says it is working constructively with SAMR; a final decision is expected between September 2026 and March 2027. The negotiation adds another copper supply-chain leverage point to Beijing's toolkit.

headline: DEUTSCHE BANK TARGETS $22,050 COPPER BY MID-2027 — STOCKPILING SCRAMBLE TO DEPLETE FREE INVENTORY AS US-CHINA RESERVES HIT 2MT
snippet: Deutsche Bank metals research head Daniel Ghali has set a $22,050/tonne copper target for Q2 2027 — roughly 50% above current LME levels of ~$14,585 — arguing that US and Chinese strategic stockpiling is depleting globally available copper inventory at a critical rate. The bank estimates China alone holds 2.05 million tonnes in strategic reserves and projects that unencumbered copper outside strategic stockpiles could approach zero by end-2028 on current trajectory. BMO has separately raised its 2030 copper forecast to $18,000/t. The call has direct implications for junior copper developers who could see project valuations reprice sharply if even a fraction of the upside materialises.

headline: UBS: GOLD SECTOR SELLOFF IS OVERDONE — WANGUO, ZIJIN, ZHAOJIN NAMED AS TOP PICKS AFTER 4-18% OCTOBER CORRECTION IN MINERS
snippet: UBS analysts published a note Monday arguing gold mining stocks have sold off beyond what the underlying bullion price decline justifies, and that the next sector rally is 'taking shape' ahead of the October 27-28 FOMC meeting. Since early September, gold mining equities have fallen 4-18% while spot gold has retreated far less from its January $5,589 peak — creating historically wide equity discounts to NAV. UBS is selective rather than broadly bullish, naming Wanguo Gold, Zijin Gold International and Zhaojin Mining as preferred exposures. For retail investors in junior gold producers, the note reinforces that the valuation gap could snap back sharply once macro uncertainty resolves.

headline: BNDES WEIGHS EQUITY STAKE IN LYNAS CALDEIRA REFINERY — BRAZIL STATE BANK EYES CO-INVESTMENT IN WORLD'S LARGEST IONIC CLAY PROJECT
snippet: Brazil's national development bank BNDES is in active discussions to participate — either through a direct loan or an equity stake via its BNDESPar arm — in Lynas Rare Earths' proposed Caldeira separation plant in Minas Gerais. This is a distinct development from the A$968M Meteoric Resources acquisition announced last week: Lynas estimates total Caldeira investment exceeds US$500 million, and BNDES involvement would signal Brazil's commitment to owning a share of rare earth processing value, not merely providing ore. Brazil's minister of mines confirmed the facility could become the largest rare earth separation plant outside China. Final terms depend on completion of the Meteoric acquisition (January 2027 shareholder vote).

headline: SMM COPPER DAILY OCT 12: PRICES RETREAT FROM HIGHS AS SUPPLY LOOSENS SLIGHTLY — CHINESE SECONDARY BUYERS STEP IN ON DIP
snippet: Shanghai Metals Market's October 12 secondary copper review notes prices retreated from recent highs as supply conditions 'marginally loosened' — providing a measured counterpoint to the Chilean-strike-driven copper bull narrative. Secondary copper rod enterprises chose to buy the dip rather than chase the rally, suggesting physical market tightness is not as acute as headline prices imply. The overnight LME rally of 1.79% was attributed partly to bear short-covering rather than fresh fundamental buying. SMM still expects copper to consolidate at elevated levels, but flags that 'high prices may be hard to sustain' absent fresh supply disruption catalysts.

headline: GOLD AT $4,220, HIGHEST IN A WEEK, AS NYSE GOES DARK FOR COLUMBUS DAY — MARKET CAUTIOUS AHEAD OF OCT 27 FOMC
snippet: Gold opened Monday at $4,220, its highest level in over a week, as Columbus Day shuttered the NYSE and left precious metals price discovery to European and Asian session participants. December futures opened up 2.3% before pulling back; Kitco reported spot gold dipping to $4,175 mid-session as profit-taking emerged. Analysts describe the session as 'wait-and-see' — Friday's surge on weak US jobs data (Fed rate-hike odds cut from 70% to below 25%) is being digested, not extended. The October 27-28 FOMC meeting remains the next binary directional catalyst for both gold and junior mining stocks.

headline: ASX LITHIUM STOCKS DUMPED AS MONDAY OPENS — PRODUCERS EXTEND SEPTEMBER LOSSES WHILE BROADER MINERS RALLY ON IRON ORE
snippet: ASX lithium producers experienced sharp Monday falls even as broader mining stocks rallied on firmer iron ore prices — extending the sector's pattern of underperformance through September and into October. Spodumene prices remain depressed near US$700/tonne, roughly 85% below 2022 peak levels. The divergence between lithium equities and the broader mining complex underscores a structural challenge for junior lithium developers: in a gold-and-copper bull market, capital continues to rotate away from lithium equity even when battery metals hold a compelling long-term demand thesis.

headline: 18 FOREIGN FIRMS — 3 FROM US — RACE FOR BRAZIL'S RARE EARTHS AS CALDEIRA AND SANTA QUITERIA EMERGE AS STRATEGIC TARGETS
snippet: At least 18 foreign companies — including three American firms — are actively pursuing Brazil's rare earth reserves as the country positions itself as the leading non-Chinese source of heavy and magnet rare earths. Brazilian officials are mobilising state financing through BNDES and the Ministry of Mines, with Lynas's Caldeira ionic clay project and CPRM's Santa Quitéria among the highest-profile assets. China's June 2026 export controls on rare earth processing chemicals have materially accelerated Western governments' urgency to diversify supply, with Brazil's large, varied and largely under-drilled rare earth deposits the most accessible alternative to Chinese dominance.
